visualTexts.title: Junior Coding Camp
visualTexts.html:
SENGKANG COMMUNITY CLUB
JUNIOR CODING CAMP
Build your first game in five days
Dates1–5 December (Mon–Fri)
Time9.30 a.m. – 12.30 p.m. daily
Age9 to 12 years
Fee$180  $120 if you sign up before 10 November
Places24 only — first come, first served
Please note
Participants must bring their own laptop. A limited number of laptops may be borrowed from the club, but these must be reserved at the counter at least one week in advance.
No prior coding experience is required.
Register at the Level 2 counter or call 6555 0148. Sibling discount of 10% applies to the second child.

questions.q: How many days does the camp run for?
A child who is eight years old wants to join. What is the problem?
options: She is below the minimum age
The camp is only for beginners

questions.q: How much would a family pay for two children who register on 3 November?
questions.tip: Two early-bird places at $120 = $240, less 10% off the second child ($12) = $228.

questions.q: What must a participant do if he does not own a laptop?
options: Reserve one at the counter at least a week early

questions.q: Which statement is true according to the poster?
options: The camp runs in the afternoon

questions.q: Why does the poster say 'first come, first served'?
options: To show the camp is free
To warn that places may run out

questions.q: What is the purpose of showing '$180' with a line through it?
options: To show the fee has been cancelled
To show the price has increased
To make the discounted price look more attractive
To show the fee for older children
questions.tip: Visual text questions often ask why a design choice was made.

questions.q: Who is this poster mainly aimed at?
questions.tip: Age range, fees and registration all point to parents.

visualTexts.title: Lift Upgrading Notice
visualTexts.html:
BLOCK 412C TOWN COUNCIL18 SEPT
LIFT B WILL BE OUT OF SERVICE
Monday 6 October to Friday 24 October
Lift B will be shut down for a full replacement of its motor and control panel. Residents should use Lift A, which will continue to run as usual.

Work will take place from 8.00 a.m. to 6.00 p.m. on weekdays only. There will be no work on Saturdays, Sundays or public holidays. Some noise and dust is unavoidable during these hours.
Residents needing assistance
Elderly residents and residents with mobility difficulties living on floors 8 and above may call the Town Council to arrange help with groceries during this period. Please give at least two days' notice.
Enquiries: 6789 2210 (Mon–Fri, 9 a.m. – 5 p.m.)
We apologise for the inconvenience and thank residents for their patience.

questions.q: How long will Lift B be out of service?
questions.tip: 6 to 24 October is three working weeks.

questions.q: What should residents do while Lift B is closed?
questions.tip: The notice says residents "should use Lift A, which will continue to run as usual" while Lift B is replaced.

questions.q: A resident hears drilling at 7.30 p.m. on a Tuesday. What can she conclude?
options: The work is running outside the stated hours
questions.tip: Work is stated as 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.

questions.q: Who may ask the Town Council for help with groceries?
options: Residents on floors 8 and above who are elderly or have mobility difficulties
Residents who call on the same day
questions.tip: Two conditions must both be met.

questions.q: A resident wants help on Friday. When is the latest she should call?
questions.tip: At least two days' notice means Wednesday at the latest.

questions.q: Why is the paragraph about assistance placed in a shaded box?
options: It is the least important information
To make it stand out for the residents it concerns
Because there was space left over
questions.tip: Design choices direct the reader's attention.

visualTexts.title: School Recycling Results
visualTexts.html:
RIVERBANK PRIMARY · TERM 3
Paper collected by level (kg)
Target for each level: 300 kg
P5 collected the most and was the only level to reach the target. P3 collected the least, but they are also the smallest level, with only three classes compared with five in every other level.

Next term: each level will be measured on kilograms per pupil instead of total kilograms.

questions.q: Which level collected the most paper?
How much paper did P4 collect?
questions.tip: The P4 bar is labelled 240, so read straight across from the P4 row to its number.

questions.q: How far below the target was P6?
Why might it be unfair to say that P3 performed worst?
options: They have fewer classes than the other levels
questions.tip: The text explains P3 has three classes, not five.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the dotted red line?
options: To divide the chart in half
To show the target of 300 kg

questions.q: Why will the school change to measuring kilograms per pupil?
options: It makes the comparison fairer between levels of different sizes
It will increase the total collected
questions.tip: This follows directly from the point made about P3.

listening.title: Listening Comprehension · Practice Paper 1
listening.instructions: A parent, sibling or friend reads each text aloud TWICE, at a normal speaking pace, with a short pause between the two readings. The child reads the question and the four options first, then listens. Do not show the child the script. 20 marks.

items.script: Attention, shoppers. The children's play area on level four will close at four o'clock today instead of the usual seven o'clock, as the flooring is being cleaned. It will reopen tomorrow morning at ten as normal. We apologise for any inconvenience.
items.q: Why is the play area closing early?

items.script: Girl: Dad, the school bus leaves at half past six tomorrow. Father: Half past six? That's twenty minutes earlier than usual. Girl: It's because of the traffic on the expressway. Mrs Lee said we should be at the pick-up point by six twenty at the latest.
items.q: What time must the girl be at the pick-up point?

items.script: The library will be running a book exchange next Saturday. Bring up to five books you have finished reading, and take home the same number that somebody else has brought. Books must be in good condition. Textbooks and magazines will not be accepted.
items.q: Which of these can a child bring to the exchange?

items.script: Boy: I've been practising the piano for an hour every day. Girl: Every day? Even on weekends? Boy: Well, not Sundays. My grandmother visits, so I stop after twenty minutes.
items.q: How long does the boy practise on Sundays?

items.script: Good morning, class. Please note that tomorrow's Science test has been moved from the second period to the fourth period. The syllabus remains exactly the same. You should still bring your practical worksheets, as we will go through them after the test.
items.q: What has changed about the Science test?

items.script: Woman: I'd like to return these shoes, please. They're the wrong size. Assistant: Certainly. Do you have the receipt? Woman: I'm afraid I've lost it. Assistant: In that case I can offer you an exchange or a store credit, but not a cash refund.
items.q: What can the woman get without a receipt?

items.script: Tomorrow's weather: cloudy in the morning with a chance of light showers before noon. The afternoon will be bright and warm, with temperatures reaching thirty-three degrees. Thundery showers are expected again in the late evening.
items.q: When is the weather expected to be best?

items.script: Boy: Are you joining the camp? Girl: I want to, but it clashes with my cousin's wedding. Boy: That's a shame. Girl: My mother says I can go to the second session in December instead.
items.q: Why can't the girl attend the camp?

items.script: Passengers are reminded that eating and drinking are not permitted anywhere on the train network, including on platforms and in station concourses. Plain water is the only exception, and only in an emergency. Offenders may be fined.
items.q: What is the only thing passengers may consume?

items.script: Girl: Did you finish the poster? Boy: Almost. I did the drawing and the title, but I've run out of green paint for the border. Girl: I have some. I'll bring it tomorrow morning before assembly.
items.q: What does the boy still need to complete?

items.script:
Good afternoon, everyone. I'm speaking to you today about our upcoming overnight camp at Pulau Ubin. We leave from the school gate at seven in the morning on the fifteenth of June and return at four in the afternoon on the sixteenth. The ferry ride takes about fifteen minutes.

You will need to bring one change of clothes, a torch, insect repellent and a refillable water bottle. Do not bring mobile phones, snacks or money. Any snacks brought will be collected and returned to you at the end of the camp, because food attracts wild boar to the campsite.

We will be cycling on the first afternoon. Helmets will be provided, but if you have your own and prefer it, you are welcome to bring it. Pupils who cannot cycle should tell Mr Rahim by Friday so that we can arrange the nature walk group instead. There is no need to feel embarrassed about this — last year, eleven pupils joined the walk.

Finally, the consent form must be signed by a parent and handed in by next Wednesday. Pupils without a signed form will not be allowed to board the ferry, even if they turn up on the day.
items.q: How long does the camp last?
options: One night only, returning the same evening

items.q: Why are snacks not allowed?
options: There is no space in the bags

items.q: What should a pupil who cannot cycle do?
options: Borrow a bicycle from a friend

items.q: Why does the speaker mention that eleven pupils joined the walk last year?
options: To show the walk is unpopular
To reassure pupils who cannot cycle
To explain why cycling was cancelled
To encourage pupils to learn to cycle

items.q: What happens to a pupil who arrives without a signed consent form?
options: He is not allowed to board the ferry

items.script:
Interviewer: Madam Siti, you have been running the hawker stall for thirty-two years. What has changed the most?

Madam Siti: The customers. When I started, almost everyone who came was from this neighbourhood. I knew their names, I knew what they ordered. Now half my customers find me on their phones, from an app. They come once, take a photograph of the food, and I never see them again.

Interviewer: Is that a bad thing?

Madam Siti: Not bad. Different. The queue is longer, which my son is very happy about. But cooking for a stranger is not the same as cooking for a neighbour. When Mr Tan came every Tuesday for eighteen years, I knew he liked extra gravy and no chilli. I did not need to ask.

Interviewer: Will your children take over the stall?

Madam Siti: My daughter is a nurse. My son says he will, but he says it the way people say things to make their mother happy. I have told him not to. It is fourteen hours a day and your back never forgives you. If he wants to cook, he should cook because he cannot stop himself, not because I did it first.
items.q: How long has Madam Siti run the stall?
What is the biggest change she describes?
Why does she mention Mr Tan?
options: He was her most difficult customer
To show how well she knew her regular customers
He is taking over the stall

items.q: How does she feel about her son taking over?
options: She has told him not to
She has already decided he will
She does not believe he can cook

items.q: What does she mean by 'he should cook because he cannot stop himself'?
options: He should cook only when hungry
He should take over out of duty
He should do it out of genuine passion, not obligation
He should learn to cook faster
